keys.statement: Choose the tear stream deliberately and add make-up streams for components lost from the loop (for example solvent losses); without them a recycled solvent loop does not close.

plain.title: Solvent loop does not close: choose the tear on purpose and add make-up streams
plain.when: A recycled solvent loop does not converge.
plain.do: Choose the tear stream (the recycle stream that is guessed and recomputed) deliberately, and add make-up streams for every component lost from the loop, such as solvent losses, calculated to close the balance.
plain.why: Losses drain the loop unless they are made up.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, check the solvent balance: make-up equals the losses in all outlets.

source.locator: Section 'Methodology for Applying Process Simulations': process modelling and simulations

decisions.obstacle: A solvent loop does not converge.
decisions.mechanism: Losses drain the loop unless made up.
decisions.operation: Pick the tear and calculate make-ups that close the balance.

keys.statement: Simulate and size each separation unit on its own first, then reach the purity or recovery target with a design specification that adjusts one variable, or a sensitivity scan, before connecting the whole process.

plain.title: Unit misses purity in the plant: fix it alone first with a design specification, then connect
plain.when: A separation unit misses its purity once connected in the plant.
plain.do: Simulate and size each separation unit alone first. Reach its purity or recovery with a design specification that adjusts one variable, or a sensitivity scan, before connecting the whole process.
plain.why: Fixing units alone separates unit problems from loop problems.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, pair each target with one free variable and bounds, and keep each run.

keys.statement: Size the diameter of packed absorbers and strippers for 60 to 80% of their flooding capacity, and the packed height from earlier studies or a height-to-diameter ratio.

plain.title: Packed absorbers and strippers: size the diameter for 60-80% of flooding
plain.when: You size a packed absorber or stripper.
plain.do: Size the diameter for 60 to 80% of the flooding capacity, and the packed height from earlier studies or a height-to-diameter ratio.
plain.why: Too close to flooding loses operability; too far wastes column.
plain.check: Check the fractional capacity at your highest vapour and liquid loads.

keys.statement: Check predictive property methods (UNIFAC- or COSMO-type) against measured data over a wide range of the property before a design relies on them.

plain.title: Predictive property method (UNIFAC- or COSMO-type): check it against data first
plain.when: A design relies on phase behaviour or properties from a predictive model, for example for ionic liquids or other unusual molecules.
plain.do: Check the method against measured data over a wide range of the property before a design relies on it.
plain.why: Group-contribution and COSMO methods can err for unusual molecules.
plain.check: Lab relies on CHEPTA's property provenance; this check matters where a method lacks data for the case's components.

keys.statement: When a regeneration column runs under vacuum, count the energy to compress its vapour back to atmospheric pressure in the utility demand.

plain.title: Regeneration under vacuum: count the vacuum compressor's energy
plain.when: A regeneration column runs under vacuum.
plain.do: Model the vacuum system as a compressor that returns the vapour to atmospheric pressure, and count its energy in the utilities.
plain.why: A vacuum system is a compressor; leaving it out makes vacuum operation look cheaper than it is.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, add a compressor on the vacuum column's vapour and include its work in the energy comparison.
